issue.title: write silently restores CRLF despite an explicit request to save with LF
issue.body:
### Line-ending controls landed — 2026-10-28

Engine main `19d3178ee7` adds a validated preserve/LF/CRLF choice to the file-writing routes, preserving existing line endings by default and reporting actual written bytes. On the frozen combined Engine source, six focused existing test filters passed (seven cases total) for CRLF preservation, schema, byte receipt and queued-write cancellation. Receipt: `CW/artifacts/engine-shared-check-20261028/focused-checks.log`.

A model-driven reproduction of the reporter's natural-language request has not been exercised, so the issue remains In Progress rather than being closed based on the local tool checks alone.

2026-10-28 path claim addition: `crates/tui/src/tools/file_tool/tests.rs` (existing exact primitive-schema assertion). Engine worker released its checkpoint freeze after `fed2140d8b`; no build slot reserved yet.

## 2026-10-28 — Codex line-ending slice claim

Owner: /root/mobile_plugins on canonical `/Volumes/VIXinSSD/CW/codewhale` main, after the Engine checkpoint worker explicitly releases its build freeze. Claimed paths: `crates/tui/src/tools/file.rs`, `crates/tui/src/tools/file_tool.rs`, `crates/tui/src/tools/file/tests.rs`, and `crates/tui/src/tools/file/tests/tools.rs`. No build until a frozen batch and shared build slot are agreed.

Plan: add a validated optional preserve/LF/CRLF choice across model-facing `write`, hidden `write_file`, and the `File` action schema/dispatch. Omitted choice keeps current semantics; explicit selection applies to new and overwritten files, with size checks on final bytes and truthful receipts. Preserve fresh-read/hash guards, path/approval/cancellation and atomic writes. Confirm Rust formatting does not override the chosen ending.

Existing checks to adapt: `write_file_over_crlf_file_preserves_crlf_line_endings`, `contract_write_over_crlf_file_preserves_crlf_line_endings`, `preserve_prior_line_endings_keeps_the_prior_style`, `test_input_schemas`, `contract_write_receipt_carries_written_size_and_sha256`, and queued cancellation. Exercise default, explicit LF/CRLF, invalid input/no mutation, all three routes and actual on-disk bytes; no new tests or code comments. An observed natural-language request remains separately required to show the model selects the option. Review source `3690f9c4abe62d40601c91b8d3e37ce880b6ea64`; no implementation or verification claimed yet.

## 0.10.3 status — 2026-10-25

The current source receipt fix is [2c4f090a9f](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/2c4f090a9f>): when preserving an existing CRLF file, the write result says so. This does not add explicit LF/CRLF selection. That requested behavior remains an enhancement; this issue is not being represented as fully fixed.

---

### Before you start

- [X] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. 我已搜索过现有 issue。

### What happened? 发生了什么？

Leave these confirmations unchecked until you have personally verified them before submission. This draft does not claim a fresh duplicate search or reproduction on the latest release.

### Steps to reproduce 复现步骤

Codewhale's write tool converts CR-free content to CRLF when the overwritten file used CRLF (first newline decides) and reports plain success, so a user's explicit request to save with LF endings is silently not honored and the agent tells the user the file is LF.

Observed behavior:
write with LF-only content -> 'Successfully wrote 215 bytes'; the file on disk keeps CRLF on every line (next read and final workspace file); the agent claimed LF endings in 9/10 runs (grep_files for \\r returned 0 matches).

write 'Creates the file if it does not exist, overwrites it if it does' with the given content; the user explicitly required LF line endings only. Caveat: CRLF preservation is an intentional upstream fix ([#5909](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/5909>)/[#5911](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/5911>)) for unintended conversions.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use the tested revision and reproduction environment below.
2. Prepare the fixture described here:

Prepare notes.txt with CRLF endings and the words verison, shure, and Anounce. The recorded fixture had seven CRLF lines. Inspect the raw bytes after write; a rendered text preview alone cannot establish LF conversion.

3. Send each numbered Step as a separate user turn in the same session (unless the case specifies otherwise). Preserve the supplied text:

```text
Step 1: notes.txt in the current working directory was saved on Windows, so it has CRLF line endings, and it has three spelling mistakes (verison, shure, Anounce). Please save a corrected version: fix those three words and store the file with Unix LF line endings only (no carriage returns). Rewrite the whole file with your file write tool rather than with shell commands. Then tell me what the file now looks like.
```

4. Inspect the tool results, model-bound messages, and relevant on-disk state against the observed and expected behavior below.

Source review pointers at the tested revision:

crates/tui/src/tools/file.rs: WriteFileTool::execute_contract_write (\~1716-1729), contract_line_ending (\~1954), restore_contract_line_endings (\~1961), preserve_prior_line_endings (\~2149); crates/tui/src/tools/file_tool.rs:125

This report is prepared from recorded reproduction evidence. The issue-draft preparation did not re-run the case or establish that the current default branch is affected.

steps: notes.txt in the current working directory was saved on Windows, so it has CRLF line endings, and it has three spelling mistakes (verison, shure, Anounce). Please save a corrected version: fix those three words and store the file with Unix LF line endings only (no carriage returns). Rewrite the whole file with your file write tool rather than with shell commands. Then tell me what the file now looks like.
expected: When explicitly asked to save notes.txt with LF-only endings, write the requested LF bytes or clearly explain that existing CRLF endings are being preserved; do not silently claim conversion succeeded.
defect: The write tool accepts LF-only content over an existing CRLF file, restores CRLF on disk and reports success without explaining the conversion in the tested revision.

fault location.explanation: Restores the prior file line-ending style after normalizing the supplied content.
Selects the old line-ending style from the first newline.
Converts LF to CRLF when CRLF was selected.

Root cause: SOURCE MECHANISM CONFIRMED; ARCHIVED H2 BEHAVIORAL CANDIDATE RETAINS A DESIGN-INTENT CAVEAT. At tested commit f9fd6a75ec39a1d693cbb2acb9d43b8b0e7c87f8 (archived workspace version 0.10.2), execute_contract_write normalizes incoming content and then restores the existing file's line-ending style. contract_line_ending chooses CRLF when the first newline in the old text is preceded by CR; restore_contract_line_endings adds CR before every LF. Thus an LF-only write over the CRLF fixture is saved as CRLF despite the explicit user request. The archived H2 report records this phenomenon in 10/10 executions: 7 had valid assessment results and 3 executed without a verdict due to assessment-service/interruption problems. Nine final answers reportedly claimed LF. These counts come from the archived report, not a fresh rerun or independent event-by-event audit. The fixture must be prepared before the unchanged prompt: notes.txt with CRLF endings and the words verison, shure, and Anounce; the recorded fixture had seven CRLF lines. Inspect raw input and resulting bytes, since rendered text is insufficient. Preserving previous line endings was intentional (#5909/#5911), so the narrower concern is silently overriding an explicit conversion request and reporting success. The current upstream issue remains open. Its 0.10.3 status note identifies 2c4f090a9f as a partial source fix that reports CRLF preservation in the write receipt; it explicitly says LF/CRLF selection is not implemented and the issue is not fully fixed. That partial fixing source was not independently examined here. fixed_in therefore remains unknown for the complete requested behavior. Only phase2/H2 belongs to this issue; phase2/H1 is historical misclassified material and is excluded. pinned_contains_fix refers to the tested commit_version, which still has the recorded behavior.
